newsitem.title: USA: US issues CPI reference numbers for indexed notes.
newsitem.headline: US issues CPI reference numbers for indexed notes.

text.p: The Treasury Department on Tuesday issued the reference Consumer Price Index numbers and daily index ratios for February to be used for calculating the return on new 10-year inflation-indexed notes.
The first auction of inflation-indexed notes is to occur on Jan 29.
Treasury said that on Feb 1 and for each day through Feb 28 it will be using a reference number for CPI of 158.60 and that the daily index ratio used to calculate return on the notes will be 1.00104.

Treasury uses the non-seasonally adjusted CPI for urban consumers, called the CPI-U, for the prior three-month period to set the reference number. The non-seasonally adjusted CPI-U in November and in December was 158.6.
Treasury will announce the reference CPI numbers and the related index ratio monthly for at least a year while traders and investors become more familiar with the new debt product.
